text: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan who live on Mount Samaria, you who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to your husbands, "Bring us something to drink!"
The Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness: Days are coming upon you when you will be carried off with hooks, the last of you with fishhooks.
You will go out through breaches in the wall, each woman straight ahead of her, and you will be cast out toward Harmon, declares the LORD.
Go to Bethel and sin; go to Gilgal and sin all the more! Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every third day.
Burn leavened bread as a thank offering, proclaim your freewill offerings for all to hear—for this is what you love, people of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.

versions.text: Burn leavened bread as a thank offering, announce your freewill offerings, make them heard—for this is what you love, people of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.
versions.explanation: "Announce ... make them heard" is redundant in English and stumbles when read aloud. Combining the two Hebrew verbs into one flowing clause preserves the sense (public proclamation of the offerings) with better oral rhythm.

text: I gave you empty stomachs in all your cities and a lack of bread in all your places, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
I also withheld the rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. I sent rain on one city and withheld it from another. One field was watered, while another withered for lack of rain.
People from two or three cities staggered to another city for water but were not satisfied, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
I struck you with blight and mildew; the locust devoured your many gardens and vineyards, your fig trees and olive trees, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.

I sent plagues among you as I did to Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, and your horses were carried away captive. I made the stench of your camps rise into your nostrils, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.

versions.text: I sent plagues among you as I did to Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, along with the horses you had captured. I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camps, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew עִם שְׁבִי סוּסֵיכֶם means "with the captivity of your horses"—the horses of Israel were taken as spoil by the enemy. The current rendering "the horses you had captured" reverses the sense, making Israel the captor rather than the victim, and turns a judgment into a description of Israel's plunder.

versions.text: I sent plagues among you as I did to Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, and your horses were carried away captive. I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camps, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb וָאַעֲלֶה is causative, "I made to go up/rise," picturing the stench ascending into the nostrils. "I filled your nostrils" conveys the sense but loses the vivid rising image and the natural subject-verb movement that reads well aloud. The existing rendering is defensible, not wrong.

text: I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. You were like a charred stick snatched from the fire, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel. Because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel!

For behold, he who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who declares to man his thoughts, who makes the dawn and the darkness, and treads upon the heights of the earth—the LORD, the God of hosts, is his name.
